rv.q: A gifted storyteller, he homes in on the human drama while retaining the magical qualities of Baum’s classic novel — a winning combination that proves to be deeply moving.
The actors’ comic portrayals of these scarecrow, tin man and lion stand-ins are multilayered delights, as are the distinct and defining signature songs Quijada has written for them.
Those qualities are in abundance in the best new play of the year - SOMEWHERE OVER THE BORDER.
This is a musical that demands theatregoers' support.

Using the framework of The Wizard of Oz and a score (also composed by Quijada) that combines cumbia, hip-hop, Mexican boleros, and pop, it’s an exhilarating, smart, and soulful show that wears its parallels to L. Frank Baum’s tale well.
His mashup of his mother's memories of crossing the border and later settling in Chicago with the "Wizard of Oz" is a masterpiece in the making.

There aren’t enough superlatives in the English language—or Spanish, for that matter—to describe this show, where every single moment captures our imagination, tickles our funny bone, or makes us want to cry.

cn.t: Critics hail this inventive musical as a triumph, praising Brian Quijada's brilliant mashup of "The Wizard of Oz" with his mother's harrowing immigrant journey from El Salvador to the U.S.
